citeAs: Rohatgi, S., Qin, Y., Aw, B., Unnithan, N., Kan, M.-Y. (2023). The ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics. arXiv:2305.14996.
creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan (Pennsylvania State University; National University of Singapore)
description: ACL OCL is a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. It includes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, and structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar. The corpus spans seven decades, containing 73,285 papers published from 1952 to September 2022, alongside 210K figures.
name: ACL OCL
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Topic classification performance was evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation on the STop dataset (80% train, 20% test). The best model (PLM-SPECTER) achieved 69% accuracy, 66% Macro F1, and 68% Weighted F1. A manual case study on the top 15 cited papers showed 87% accuracy (13/15 correct). Full-text quality was manually assessed on 21 documents, revealing issues with missing sections (19 sections not detected), footnote concatenation (25/92 footnotes missing), figure detection (28.78% not detected), and table detection (31.58% not detected, 46.06% detected with errors).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Topic labels were obtained by crawling published papers from online CL conferences (ACL 2020, EMNLP 2020, ACL-IJCNLP 2021, EACL 2021, NAACL 2021) along with their author-submitted topic labels from conference websites. These 2,545 labeled papers (STop dataset) were used to train a supervised PLM-based topic classifier. Silver topic labels for the full OCL corpus were then generated by the trained model.
rai:dataBiases: The corpus is limited to peer-reviewed CL papers from the ACL Anthology, which may not represent all CL research. English is the dominant language, with many low-resource languages underrepresented. Silver topic labels exhibit bias toward dominant topics (e.g., Machine Translation), as evidenced by the higher accuracy on top-cited papers (87%) compared to the overall test set (69%). The topic classification model was trained on papers from 2020–2021 conferences only, which may not generalize to older papers.
rai:dataCollection: Crawlers were designed to fetch all PDF documents and metadata from the ACL Anthology website. Metadata is sourced from the website (author-driven, more accurate than PDF extraction). PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed (mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks). The dataset undergoes annual updates by downloading and processing papers recently added to the ACL Anthology, identifying new additions by monitoring changes in URLs.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF files and metadata crawled from the ACL Anthology website (https://aclanthology.org/), covering 73,285 conference, journal, and workshop papers in the CL domain published from 1952 to September 2022.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Papers published from 1952 to September 2022; data collected and processed up to 2022.
rai:dataLimitations: OCL is a small-scale collection focused only on peer-reviewed, open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology; it does not include CL papers from other sources (e.g., arXiv cs.CL). Full-text extraction quality is limited by GROBID's constraints, particularly for formatting information such as figures, tables, and inline equations. Only open-source PDF extraction tools were used due to budget constraints. The corpus is largely unlabeled, lacking annotations for specific tasks. Silver topic labels are model-predicted and may contain errors (69% accuracy on test set).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is provided in both standard CSV format and Apache Parquet (open-source, column-oriented data format) to facilitate efficient downstream processing. Silver topic labels were generated by a trained PLM-based neural model (PLM-SPECTER) and integrated into the corpus as the predicted_topic field.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Full-text extraction from PDF files was performed using GROBID. The S2ORC-JSON format was adopted for the full-text schema. Figures and tables were extracted using PDFFigures 2.0. Language detection was performed using a public language detection toolkit (langdetect by Shuyo, 2010) using title and abstract as inputs. PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed. Metadata from ACL Anthology was used in preference to PDF-extracted metadata due to higher accuracy.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which newly added papers from the ACL Anthology are downloaded and processed. New additions are identified by monitoring changes in URLs. The ultimate goal is to provide full-text extraction and information extraction APIs to ACL Anthology, hosting the OCL data on ACL Anthology itself.
rai:dataSocialImpact: ACL OCL advances open science in computational linguistics by providing accessible and standardized data resources, promoting reproducibility in research. The corpus enables analysis of research trends, including the emergence of new topics like "Ethics of NLP" and the representation of low-resource languages. The paper notes that numerous languages remain underrepresented in the ACL Anthology, with significant disparity in coverage even among languages in the same language group.
rai:dataUseCases: Temporal topic trend analysis; document-level information extraction; related work generation; figure caption generation; multimodal research; citation network analysis; knowledge graph construction; pre-training or fine-tuning scientific language models; historical language change analysis; paper-reviewer matching; emerging topic detection; section-wise NLP tasks (contribution extraction, future work prediction); bibliographic research and metadata analysis.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID (for full-text extraction from PDFs); PDFFigures 2.0 (for figure and table extraction); langdetect library (Shuyo, 2010) for language detection; PLM-SPECTER fine-tuned classifier for automatic topic label prediction (silver labels); Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) API for citation and metadata enrichment.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: No per-item annotation count described; topic labels are single model-predicted labels, not multiple independent annotations per item.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No human annotators used; topic labels come from author-submitted conference metadata and model predictions, not crowd-sourced annotation.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform used; topic labels were crawled from conference websites, not collected via an annotation platform.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No explicit discussion of missing data handling beyond removing PDFs longer than 50 pages; full-text extraction failures are noted but not treated as a missing data protocol.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described for missing values in the dataset.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Dataset consists of published scientific papers; no personal or sensitive information beyond publicly available author names and affiliations.
